cards.narration: Jo orders a pizza for lunch. Jo and one friend share it fairly. Two people share, so each gets 1/2 of the pizza.
Now a pizza the same size is shared by 4 friends. Each friend gets 1/4 of it. The pizza is cut into 4 equal parts.
Which share is bigger, 1/2 or 1/4? When more people share, the parts are smaller. So 1/4 is less than 1/2.
Try 2, 3 and 6 sharers on same-size pizzas. Shares are 1/2, 1/3 and 1/6. From least to greatest, they go 1/6, 1/3, 1/2.
The bigger the bottom number, the smaller the share. This only works when the wholes are the same size. Fair shares need equal parts.
cards.text: More sharers means a smaller share

cards.narration: You can now compare fair shares. Think about how many people share each whole. Ready to practise?

items.narration: Two pizzas are the same size. One is shared by 2 friends. The other is shared by 4 friends. Where does each friend get more: shared by 4, or shared by 2?
items.why: Fewer sharers means bigger parts. Sharing by 2 gives 1/2 each. Sharing by 4 gives only 1/4 each.

items.narration: Two same-size subs are shared fairly. Which share is greater, 1/3 or 1/6?
items.why: Three sharers get bigger parts than six sharers. So 1/3 is greater than 1/6.

items.narration: A sub is shared fairly by 8 friends. Each friend gets 1 out of how many equal parts? Type the number.
items.why: Each of the 8 friends gets one equal part. The sub has 8 equal parts, so each share is 1/8.

items.narration: Here are 8 cookies. Two friends share them fairly. How many cookies does each friend get?
items.why: Share the cookies into 2 equal groups. 8 ÷ 2 = 4, so each friend gets 4 cookies.

items.narration: A pizza is shared fairly so each friend gets 1/4. Slide the frog to the number of friends sharing.
items.why: The bottom number tells how many equal parts there are. A share of 1/4 means 4 friends share.

items.narration: Three same-size subs are shared. One is shared by 3 friends, one by 5 friends, and one by 10 friends. Who gets the least: 3 friends, 5 friends, or 10 friends?
items.why: The most sharers make the smallest parts. Sharing by 10 gives 1/10 each. That is less than 1/5 or 1/3.

items.narration: Which list goes from least to greatest? Is it 1/8 then 1/4 then 1/2, or 1/2 then 1/4 then 1/8?
items.why: More sharers make smaller shares. So 1/8 is least, then 1/4, then 1/2 is greatest.

items.narration: One pizza is shared by 5 friends. A same-size pizza is shared by 10 friends. The smaller share is 1 out of how many parts? Type the number.
items.why: Ten sharers get smaller parts than five sharers. So the smaller share is 1/10, and the number is 10.

items.narration: Here are 12 pizza slices. Six friends share them fairly. How many slices does each friend get?
items.why: Make 6 equal groups from the slices. 12 ÷ 6 = 2, so each friend gets 2 slices.

items.narration: Lee's share of a pizza is more than 1/6 but less than 1/4. Slide the frog to the number of friends sharing.
items.why: The share must be between 1/6 and 1/4. Only 1/5 fits, so 5 friends share.

items.narration: Three same-size pizzas are shared. Mia's is shared by 3 friends. Kai's is shared by 5. Dev's is shared by 4. Whose share is in the middle in size: Mia, Kai, or Dev?
items.prompt: Whose share is in the middle?
items.why: The shares are 1/3, 1/5 and 1/4. From least to greatest: 1/5, 1/4, 1/3. Dev's 1/4 is in the middle.

items.narration: Ravi thinks 1/6 is greater than 1/3 because 6 is greater than 3. The wholes are the same size. Is Ravi right? Tap: No, he is not right, or Yes, he is right.
items.why: A bigger bottom number means more parts, so each part is smaller. 1/6 is less than 1/3, so Ravi is not right.

items.narration: A pizza is shared by 10 friends. A same-size pizza is shared by 2 friends. One share from the second pizza equals how many shares from the first? Type the number.
items.why: Split each half into tenths. The whole has 10 parts, and a half is 5 of them. So 1/2 equals 5 shares of 1/10.

items.narration: Pizza A is shared by 3 friends. Pizza B is the same size. Each friend at B gets half as much as a friend at A. Slide the frog to the number of friends at B.
items.why: A share at A is 1/3. Half of 1/3 is 1/6. So 6 friends share pizza B.

items.narration: Pizza A is shared by 8 friends. Pizza B is the same size. Each friend at B gets twice as much as a friend at A. Slide the frog to the number of friends at B.
items.why: A share at A is 1/8. Twice that is 2/8, which is the same as 1/4. So 4 friends share pizza B.
